title: Crown and Salt
premise: Paloma Zhou, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics she carves, has survived five years in Saltmere, a free city where magic is outlawed and informers are paid by the head. When a mute child arrives at her door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Paloma discovers the child carries the true name of the drowned god beneath the sea — a secret the usurper Kaelen Voss will burn every free city to possess. Hunted across salt marshes and sunken temples with a disgraced inquisitor who once hunted people like her, Paloma learns her own hearing of the dead is not a curse but an inheritance from the last priestesses. In the end, Paloma must choose between destroying the name forever — silencing the dead she loves — or speaking it aloud to raise the drowned god against Voss's armies, knowing that power freely accepted always corrupts its bearer; she speaks it, but binds the god to her own mortality, saving the free cities at the cost of her long life and winning, at last, a place to belong.
about_author: Elodie Vane is a former maritime archaeologist who spent a decade cataloguing drowned temples before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about ordinary craftspeople caught in the machinery of history, and lives in a coastal town where the fog rolls in like a debt collector.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Bones
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. We meet her carving charms in Saltmere's night market, haggling with fishwives while listening to the dead whisper through whalebone and knucklebone. She hides her gift carefully. Emotional beat: weary loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A mud-caked child appears at her door, mute except for words in a language that makes her carved bones sing painfully. The child clutches a fragment of drowned temple stone. Emotional beat: fear curdling into reluctant protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Informers Buy
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Wardens raid her street following an anonymous tip. She hides the child in her bone-dust cellar and hears, through a confiscated charm, the warden describe 'a speaker of the First Tongue.' Emotional beat: paranoia tightening around a fragile new bond.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Confession
chapters.summary: Seren Oduya's POV. A disgraced inquisitor, exiled for refusing to burn a child years ago, recognizes the First Tongue when he interrogates a smuggler. He seeks out Paloma not to arrest her but because he cannot carry what he knows alone. Emotional beat: guilt seeking absolution.

chapters.title: Salt and Ashes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Seren reveals the usurper Voss has razed two coastal villages searching for something called the Drowned Name. Paloma realizes the child fled one of them. They agree to flee together before dawn. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance forged in shared shame.

chapters.title: The Marsh Road
chapters.summary: Seren's POV. The trio crosses the Sedge Marshes; the child, whom Paloma names Wren, begins trusting Seren. Dead soldiers' bones in the mire speak to Paloma of an ancient war between the god below and the kings above. Emotional beat: tentative found-family warmth amid danger.

chapters.title: A Market of Relics
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In the free city of Brackwater they seek a translator among relic-dealers. An old dealer recognizes the temple stone and warns them: those who hear the dead are descended from the priestesses Voss's order exterminated. Emotional beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Seren's POV. To cross the border they must bribe a captain, and the price is one of Paloma's speaking-bones — a relic holding her grandmother's voice. Paloma pays it. Emotional beat: grief as currency; survival's cost made literal.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Wren finally speaks comprehensibly: the priests of the drowned god hid the god's true name inside a living child — inside Wren. Voss wants the child alive. Emotional beat: horror and tenderness entwined; the burden becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Court
chapters.summary: Voss's POV (interlude). In his conquered capital, Voss consults a chained bone-reader and reveals his motive: he heard the dead once too, as a starving boy, and was punished for it. He means to own the god's power or die trying. Emotional beat: villainy rooted in wounded belonging.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: Seren's POV. Voss's riders catch them at a river ford. Seren kills for the first time since his exile and is shaken; Wren uses a word of the First Tongue that drowns three soldiers. The child's power terrifies everyone, including Wren. Emotional beat: innocence lost on all sides.

chapters.title: The Sunken Temple
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Guided by the dead, they reach a half-drowned temple where priestess-ghosts recognize Paloma's gift and teach her the grammar of the First Tongue. They warn: the name can be spoken only once, by one voice, and it changes the speaker forever. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: What Seren Buried
chapters.summary: Seren's POV. Seren confesses he was the inquisitor who signed the order that destroyed Paloma's home village years ago — the reason her family died. Paloma's trust shatters. Emotional beat: betrayal, rage, and the question of whether love survives truth.

chapters.title: The Broken Road
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma walks out alone into a storm, ready to abandon them both, but the dead beg her to return — Wren is crying for her in the First Tongue. She chooses to go back, though forgiveness waits. Emotional beat: choosing connection over self-protection.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. His armies march on the free cities; his chained bone-reader dies giving him the temple's location. Voss burns a hostage village to flush out witnesses. Emotional beat: corruption accelerating — power devouring its own humanity.

chapters.title: The Council of Free Cities
chapters.summary: Seren's POV. In Brackwater, the free cities' council refuses to believe the threat without proof. Paloma lets the council hear their own honored dead through her carved bones — exposing her gift publicly and making herself a target. Emotional beat: courage as self-sacrifice; belonging offered at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Informers and Fire
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A council member sells them out; Voss's vanguard storms Brackwater. In the chaos, Wren is captured. Seren is gravely wounded holding the gate so civilians can flee. Emotional beat: despair, and the hard arithmetic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Drowned Gate
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following the ghosts into the flooded catacombs beneath Voss's war camp, Paloma infiltrates to reach Wren, using the dead as her eyes and army. She finds Voss waiting — he wanted her to come. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Voices, One Name
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV (climax). Voss offers Paloma partnership: together they could command the god instead of serving it. She sees her own hunger for power reflected in him — and refuses. As his soldiers close in, she takes Wren's hands and speaks the Drowned Name with the child. Emotional beat: the ultimate temptation refused; the irrevocable choice made.

chapters.title: The Sea Remembers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The drowned god rises; the sea swallows Voss's armies, and Voss himself, hearing at last every dead voice he silenced, goes under screaming. The god turns to Paloma, bound now to her mortal lifespan, and subsides back into the deep. Emotional beat: victory laced with mourning.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Brackwater
chapters.summary: Seren's POV. Recovering, Seren helps rebuild; the free cities repeal the magic ban, and speakers of the dead come out of hiding. Seren asks nothing of Paloma but the chance to earn back trust slowly. Emotional beat: humility, patience, fragile hope.

chapters.title: Crown and Salt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma opens a workshop in Brackwater teaching bone-carving to the newly unhidden speakers, with Wren as her first apprentice. Her hair has gone white — the god's price — but the dead are quiet now, at peace. Emotional beat: belonging earned, survival paid for, power relinquished; home at last.
